key_insight: Recurrent neural networks trained for free recall do not just replicate one classical memory theory—they independently discover multiple human-like recall strategies. The best models use an index-based mechanism, similar to a memory palace, rather than only a simple temporal context signal.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to model human free recall more realistically, especially the challenge of explaining why people use different memory strategies instead of a single uniform process.
method: Train recurrent neural networks on free-recall tasks and analyze the strategies they develop.
Compare the learned behaviors against classical temporal context models and human recall patterns.
Identify and characterize top-performing models, including an index-based mechanism resembling mnemonic techniques.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that optimization can produce richer, more interpretable memory systems than hand-designed assumptions alone. It also suggests new directions for building recall-capable models that better match human memory behavior.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison diagram: classical temporal context model vs. learned RNN strategies

paper_title: A neural network model of free recall learns multiple memory strategies
paper_authors: Moufan Li, Kristopher T. Jensen, Qiong Zhang, Qihong Lu, Marcelo G. Mattar
